aliases: Prof. Dr. Dr.-Ing. e. h. Friedrich Robert Helmert
name: Friedrich Robert Helmert
summary: Founder of modern geodesy and long-serving director of the Royal Prussian Geodetic Institute.

name: Christian August Nagel
summary: Professor at the Royal Polytechnic College of Dresden and Helmert's teacher and mentor.

name: Carl Christian Bruhns
summary: Director of the astronomical observatory at the University of Leipzig and arc measurement commissioner.

name: Johann Jacob Baeyer
summary: General and head of the Trigonometric Department of the Prussian General Staff who conceived the Central European Arc Measurement.

name: Wilhelm Foerster
summary: Director of the Berlin Observatory and supporter of the Geodetic Institute.

name: Ernst Heinrich Bruns
summary: Mathematician, physicist and astronomer who contributed to theoretical geodesy and the definition of the geoid.

name: Royal Prussian Geodetic Institute
summary: Scientific institute for geodesy, initially in Berlin and later relocated to Potsdam.

name: Central Bureau of the Internationale Erdmessung
summary: International organization for geodesy, forerunner of the International Association of Geodesy.

name: Royal Polytechnic College of Dresden
summary: Educational institution in Dresden where Helmert studied engineering sciences.

name: University of Leipzig
summary: University where Helmert earned his PhD in 1868.

name: Hamburg Observatory
summary: Observatory where Helmert worked as an observer from 1869 to 1870.

name: Royal Rhine-Westphalia Polytechnic College in Aachen
summary: Educational institution where Helmert served as a professor from 1870 to 1885.

name: Prussian Academy of Sciences
summary: Academy to which Helmert was elected as a full member in 1899.

name: Freiberg
summary: Town in Saxony where Helmert was born.

name: Potsdam
summary: City where the Geodetic Institute was located and where Helmert died.

aliases: Die Mathematischen und Physikalischen Theorien der Höheren Geodäsie
name: Mathematical and Physical Theories of Higher Geodesy
summary: Helmert's two-volume work published in 1880 and 1884 on the theories of geodesy.

name: Potsdam Gravity System
summary: International gravity reference system adopted in 1909 based on measurements at Potsdam.

name: Helmert Tower
summary: Tower at the Geodetic Institute in Potsdam used for angle measurements and later satellite triangulations.
